channel.title: TextMate 3
channel.description: Application updates for TextMate 3. Empty until the first release ships. Items are added by the release pipeline and signed with the production EdDSA key.

item.title: TextMate 2.1.0-alpha.2
item.description: • Two fixes from the first alpha: fetch tags with force, and zip without extended attributes (#20)

item.title: TextMate 2.1.0-alpha.1
item.description:
• The Legal page names what the application is made of (#19)
  • Markdown lint
  • A release pipeline with alpha, beta and release channels (#18)
  • Notarize on request, and sign Sparkle's Autoupdate helper as itself (#17)
  • Run the workflow once per push (#16)
  • The privileged helper as an SMAppService daemon, retiring the last deprecated call (#15)
  • Sign with a Developer ID, and re-sign the vendored Sparkle pieces with the same identity (#14)
  • Give the application its own identity, with a first launch import from TextMate 2 (#13)
  • Record the bundle editor forms and the parser deletion in the changelog (#12)
  • Delete the OpenStep ASCII property list parser and Ragel (#11)
  • Edit preferences and macros as forms in the bundle editor (#10)
  • Edit themes as a form with a live preview in the bundle editor (#9)
  • Grammar editor: panel edits reach the preview, rule shapes change, capture patterns in the outline (#8)
  • Grammar editor: live preview of sample text parsed with the grammar being edited (#7)
  • Grammar editor: add, remove and move rules, captures and repository names (#5)
  • Grammar editor: rules as an outline and a form, in place of the text pane (#4)
  • GrammarSchema: the grammar format as data, with a validator (#3)
  • Swift Testing under script/test (#2)
  • swift format's default two space indentation for the Swift sources
  • Swift and SwiftUI spike: ApplicationInfo, the About page, and the encoding chooser sheet (#1)
  • Rename LICENSE to LICENSE.md
  • Reformat LICENSE as Markdown
  • Record the removed gtm options in the changelog
  • Drop gtm's --trim and --delimiters options, which were parsed and never implemented
  • Pass .tbd library paths through in the test link too, which still prefixed them with -l
  • Record the property list caches and the end of the Homebrew run time dependency in the changelog
  • Remove Cap'n Proto: the schemas, the compiler step in bin/rave, the configure checks, the Brewfile line, and Homebrew's library directory from the linker search path
  • Link the SDK's sqlite by path in DocumentWindow and OakAppKit, so a Homebrew sqlite on the search path is never picked up
  • Drop the library validation entitlement from the command line tools, which load nothing foreign now, and say why the application still needs it for an ad hoc build
  • Store the encoding classifier's frequency tables as a binary property list, EncodingFrequencies.plist
  • Store the bundle index cache as a binary property list, BundlesIndex.plist, and read it back the same way in the application and gtm
  • Remove the cache format benchmark tool now that the format is chosen, keeping the launch measurement in script/benchmark_bundle_index
  • Left align the text columns of the benchmark report tables
  • Record the bundle index benchmark in the changelog
  • Report the first index build apart from the later ones, since it pays the process warmup a launch pays elsewhere
  • Add script/benchmark_bundle_index, which builds and runs the cache format and launch measurements and prints the report
  • Report bundle index cache load, index build and whole launch timings on stderr when TEXTMATE_BUNDLES_INDEX_TIMING is set, with TEXTMATE_BUNDLES_INDEX_PATH pointing the cache elsewhere
  • Add bundle_index_benchmark, a tool that times the bundle index cache in Cap'n Proto, property list, JSON, JSON Lines, CSV and YAML forms
  • Move the bundle index content filter from BundlesManager into the bundles framework as prune_bundle_item_plist
  • Split the bundle index cache's property list form out of load and save as to_plist and from_plist
  • Move the gtm tag to the commit each upload was built from
  • Ship gtm inside the application and publish it from continuous integration as the gtm prerelease
  • Sign gtm with the helper entitlements, so the hardened runtime lets it load the Homebrew libraries and it starts
